name: Expo (React Native)
summary: A toolkit for building an iPhone and Android app with React, sharing one JavaScript codebase between both.

free_plan_covers.note: Free plan includes 15 iOS and 15 Android cloud builds a month, plus over-the-air updates for up to 1,000 monthly active users.

first_paid_usd_month.note: Starter plan is $19 a month, with $45 of build credit and updates for up to 3,000 monthly active users.

portability.note: Prebuild regenerates the native ios and android folders any time, so you can leave Expo's managed workflow for plain React Native.

language.note: Expo apps are React Native apps, written in TypeScript or JavaScript.

shares_react_skills.note: Expo is a React Native framework, so components, hooks and JSX carry over from a React web app.

needs_mac_for_ios.note: EAS Build compiles iOS apps on a cloud macOS VM, so you can build and submit to the App Store without owning a Mac.

setup.step: Create the app with npx create-expo-app@latest.
Run npx expo start and scan the QR code with the Expo Go app on your phone to preview it live.
Install EAS CLI, run eas login and eas build:configure, then eas build to create a real installable app in the cloud.
Submit the build to the App Store or Google Play with eas submit.

builder_notes: Never put secret keys in EXPO_PUBLIC_ environment variables. They compile into the app in plain text and are readable by anyone who inspects the build.
Call anything that needs a private key from your own backend, not directly from the Expo app.
Use EAS Secrets for build-time credentials like signing keys, but treat anything bundled into the JavaScript as public.
